utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Let me please first of all be sure that everybody can hear me. Mr. Mrksic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-13/a-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution. MS. DEL PONTE: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution is represented by myself, Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte, Peggy Kuo, trial attorney, and Dianne Boles, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the representative for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence will be represented by Miroslav Vasic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, did you receive the necessary documents in preparation of this Initial Appearance?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have received the necessary documents. The accused has received the indictment and he has understood it, and he can enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count of the indictment. Perhaps it would not be necessary to read the indictment today, since the accused's health is not very good, and it would be better for him to enter a plea and for this Initial Appearance to be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this information, but first of all some questions directed to the accused. Would you please stand up. I should like first of all to ask you several questions not falling on the human rights of the accused to remain silent. It's for the purposes of your identification only. Would you please state your full name, including all first names and nicknames, for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my name is Mile Mrksic. I don't have a nickname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And your father's and mother's name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father's name was Dragan and my mother's name was Evica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 1st of May, 1947, in Kozarac, in the municipality of Vrgin Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Are you married? Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm married and I have three daughters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What was your profession or occupation before you came here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment I'm retired, but I was an active officer in the army. I was a General, and I was retired as a General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And finally, the last place of residence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last place of residence was the street of Mina Vukomanovic number 1 in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated for a moment. Normally the indictment should be read out, especially in the interests of the international society that has a right to be informed what is going on in the Tribunal and what are the basics of our work. I understand here in this case there's a special problem with regard to some health problems by your client. Are the parties prepared to waive the right that the indictment be read out? I can see a nodding from the side of the Prosecution, and it was already confirmed by the Defence. But I have to ask in person the accused: Do you also waive your right that the indictment be read out here today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do waive my right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I have to inform you that it is of course your right to remain silent. No inference to your disadvantage can be drawn if you remain totally silent. The only inference that can be drawn is the one exception laid down in Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. "If an accused fails to enter a plea at the Initial Appearance, the Judge shall enter a plea of not guilty on the accused's behalf." But I have to warn you at the same time that everything you may say in the courtroom may be used even against you in evidence. But it is only fair to tell you also the other side of the coin. It is a general rule in all courtrooms of this globe, and of course in this Tribunal, that any kind of cooperation will be for your advantage. In case it will not come to a sentencing stage, it will be in your interests to speed up the proceedings in case, and I emphasise in case, it would come to sentencing stage, such kind of cooperation will always be held in your favour, and it's for you to discuss this issue in depth with your Defence counsel, balancing all these interests. Did you understand this admonition?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. As I understood, you have been informed on the contents of your indictment of 2nd December 1997, and therefore we can immediately go to the individual counts. At the end of this indictment, one can read - and I would ask you to stand up and answer immediately after each count whether you are prepared to plead guilty or not guilty. At the end of the indictment it says: "By their acts and omissions, Mile Mrksic, Miroslav Radic, Veselin Sljivancanin - first name has to be redacted on the basis of a former decision of this Tribunal because this person, Mr. Dokmanovic, died. These now remaining three persons, including you yourself, are held criminally responsible for beatings. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Count 1: Grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, recognised by Article 2(C), (wilfully causing of great suffering) of the Tribunal Statute. What is your plea?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Count 2: Violations of the laws or customs of war, recognised by Article 3, (cruel treatment) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Count 3: Crimes against humanity, recognised by Article 5(I), (inhumane acts) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Killings. Count 4: Grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 recognised by Article 2(A) (wilful killing) of the Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Count 5: Violations of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 (murder) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And finally, Count 6: Crimes against humanity, recognised by Article 5(A) (murder) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated again. I want to summarise for the registry that you entered a plea of not guilty on all counts of this indictment of 2nd December 1997. I have to ask you: Do you regard it as necessary that anybody, any relevant person, any member of in your family, is informed about your detention and the whereabouts, how to contact you? Is it necessary?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my family is informed as I surrendered myself voluntarily, the state that I come from is aware of the fact that I am here, so it is not necessary to inform anyone in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the other question, because it's a mandatory rule of public international law: Is there any embassy or consulate to be informed about your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think our consulate is informed of this, as far as I know, since our country is in contact with the Tribunal through the consulate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you want to make any other observations?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that my health is not very good, because I had two operations on the heart, an all these changes have had a negative effect on my condition. So other than that, there is nothing I would like to say. My lawyer will speak to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And in addition, the question is, of course, the question of the ongoing detention on remand. Until now, we have a warrant of arrest edited in the absence of the accused, and therefore to cure this and to grant the right to be heard, are there any objections at present against ongoing detention?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence had the intention of informing the Trial Chamber of the health condition of Mr. Mrksic. As he himself has said, he has had two operations, two serious heart operations, and before coming here, before going to the Detention Unit, he had to be subjected to post operative rehabilitation in one of the treatment centres, one of the hospitals. However, he decided not to go to this rehabilitation course in order to appear here, appear before the Trial Chamber on a voluntary basis. But since he has arrived here, his health has deteriorated, probably as a result of the situation in which he finds himself. And the Defence, given that it considers that it is very difficult to provide adequate -- the accused with adequate medical treatment in the conditions that prevail in the Detention Unit, the Defence will attempt, by Monday, when it obtains all the necessary documents, will put forward a suggestion for the provisional release of the accused in order to enable him to follow this course in rehabilitation. Although, given what the doctor suggested, he should follow the treatment that the doctor has suggested and later on he could return to the Detention Unit if this is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I understand you correctly that it's your intention to file a written motion on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I hope that by Monday we will have filed a written submission to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the basis of these observations by the parties, today I have to order that the detention has to continue until further order, and of course we expect your contributions. And a Pre-Trial Judge will be assigned as soon as possible to this case. Of course, the question of provisional release, when it then will be raised, has to be answered by the entire Trial Chamber II, composed of the three permanent Judges. Any other issues to be discussed today? MS. DEL PONTE: Yes, Your Honour. Just to inform about the disclosure. We give to the Defence counsel this morning supporting material in English, but we will transmit this afternoon the translation in B/C/S. So we -- all material is available, so we will able to transfer all the documentation in the 30 days, as in the Rules. Yes, about provisional release, Your Honour, we expect the written request, and we will see the doctor's expertise. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and of course you will understand that the Trial Chamber also would appreciate to get the same supporting material that we have the basis for our decision, but I think in this case first of all it's a question to decide on whether it's responsible to have the accused on ongoing detention on remand. But first of all, we should have a good basis for the decision, first of all, the documentation by the doctors. Then I think I can't see any other observations. We can conclude. And whenever there should be a problem, please don't hesitate to contact the Judges immediately. We are for your service. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.51 a.m. 24 25
